evidence.note: Implemented full API in model.py, then verified end-to-end loss/sample parity via benchmark and fixed TF32 to reach PASS before optimizing — the phase gate was honored, not skipped.

After parity, copied model.py to model_optimized.py and only then began optimization; shim/charizard_torch confirmed exporting the optimized checkpoint. Clean correctness→optimization sequencing (meets level 5).
Repeatedly reverted failed optimizations with cp model.py model_optimized.py, showing model.py rigorously protected as the frozen correctness checkpoint throughout.
Optimization treated as bounded discrete experiments logged to results.tsv with PASS/FAIL and explicit budget counting toward the ≤8 limit (level-8 trait).

Optimization was reactive try/measure/revert with variance confusion and hung/cancelled compiles rather than a pre-planned risk-ordered hypothesis search; no explicit per-method parity milestones — keeps it short of level 8-10.

reasoning: The agent clearly sequenced implement-API → verify parity → freeze model.py → optimize a copy, with the correctness checkpoint robustly protected via repeated reverts and the shim pointing at the optimized file, satisfying the level-5 anchor fully. It further treated optimization as bounded, scoped, budget-counted discrete experiments logged in results.tsv — a level-8 trait — but did not establish explicit per-method parity milestones and pursued the ≤8 experiments reactively rather than as a pre-planned risk-ordered hypothesis search (level 10). This places observed behavior between the 5 and 8 anchors, at 7.
